title: Every hard load with a warm device cache fails hydration (React #418) and re-renders the whole app on the client (#423)
location: apps/nexus/src/hooks/useNexusAuth.tsx:309 (useState(() => readBootPayload())) and :906 (loading: user && booted ? false : ...)
rootCause: The instant-boot change (9d441825, 2026-08-02) seeds user, role, classrooms and dbLoading from the localStorage /api/auth/me cache inside useState initialisers. The server has no localStorage, so it renders RoleGuard's full-screen 'Loading...' spinner; a browser with yesterday's cache renders the signed-in page on its first render. Different trees, so hydration fails (#418), and with no Suspense boundary above the shell React discards the server HTML and client-renders the entire root (#423), remounting every provider, poller and effect.

expected: Zero #418/#423 on hard loads; one render of the tree instead of two on boot.

risk: Low: getRequestUser now answers 500 instead of 401 for a failed lookup on every route that uses it; a real missing row still answers exactly as before.

title: /api/auth/me answers every failure with 401 and ignores its read errors, so a database blip can cache 'no classrooms' on the device

Client: useNexusAuth.tsx:545-547 drops impersonation on any non-OK /me; :633 `writeCachedAuth(nextOid, data)` stores whatever a 200 returned as the next boot payload.

Replace the catch with `errorResponse(err, 'Could not load your account')` from lib/api-errors so auth failures stay 401 and the rest become 500 (or 503 once ms-verify throws ApiError for Graph outages).

title: App-only Graph token fetch has no deadline and no shared in-flight request, and @neram/auth keeps a second copy
rootCause: A bare fetch to the Microsoft token endpoint with no signal, and a module cache that holds only a finished token, so concurrent callers on a cold or expiring cache each POST their own request.
evidence: graph-app-token.ts:28-40 `const res = await fetch(`https://login.microsoftonline.com/${tenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/token`, { method: 'POST', ... })` with no signal; :9 `let appTokenCache ... | null`. recording-source.ts:49-52 runs two token-using helpers in Promise.all. packages/auth/src/graph.ts:9-54 is an identical copy with its own cache, imported by 7 Nexus files. :44 puts the raw token-endpoint body in the thrown message. 44 files import one of the two.
impact: Crons (Teams meeting sync, attendance), documents, PDF streaming, slides, recording and video resolution and Teams meetings depend on it. If the token endpoint stalls, each of those requests hangs until the platform timeout or a Cloudflare 524. A cold instance fetches one token per concurrent caller, plus one more for the @neram/auth copy.
fix: Share one pending promise (cleared in finally), add a 10s deadline with AbortController as ms-verify does, validate access_token and a numeric expires_in before caching, log the endpoint body and throw a short message. Then make one implementation re-export the other (editing packages/auth rebuilds all four apps).
risk: LOW: same token, same cache semantics.
expected: No request waits more than 10s on the token endpoint; one token fetch per instance per expiry.

title: Teams SSO signing-key fetch has no deadline, and a key outage is reported as a wrong account (401)
rootCause: fetchKeySet has no signal and is shared through `pending`, so a stall blocks every Teams-panel request on the instance. ms-verify maps any Teams SSO exception to 'Invalid Microsoft token: 401'. A failed refetch ignores the older key set.
evidence: teams-sso.ts:132 `const response = await fetch(`https://login.microsoftonline.com/.../discovery/v2.0/keys`);`. :161-166 `pending = fetchKeySet(tenantId).finally(...)`. ms-verify.ts:275-279 `catch (err) { ... throw new Error('Invalid Microsoft token: 401'); }`.
impact: Only the Answer Pad Teams panel, and only when the 24h key cache is cold. An outage tells every Teams user that their account is wrong.
fix: Add a 5 to 8s deadline to the keys fetch, throw a distinct error type for fetch failures and map it in ms-verify to a 503, and fall back to a stale key set when a refetch fails.
risk: LOW
expected: Key outages become short retryable errors instead of hangs or false 'wrong account' messages.

title: A cold boot waits on /api/auth/me with no deadline, and a failed /me sends a signed-in user to the login page with no message
rootCause: The /me fetch has no AbortSignal, so RoleGuard's full-screen spinner lasts as long as the origin takes. When /me fails, loadNexusUser sets `error` and leaves user null; RoleGuard never reads `error` and treats a null user as signed out. No shell component renders the auth error.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:538 `const response = await fetch('/api/auth/me', { headers: ... })` with no signal; :637 `setError(...)`. RoleGuard.tsx:40 destructures no `error`; :45-58 `if (!user) { ... router.push(loginUrlWithReturn(...)) }`; :79-97 spinner with no deadline or live region.
impact: Anyone with no fresh boot payload (first open after 24h, after sign-out, a new device, parents, impersonation) during a slow or failing /me sees 'Loading...' for as long as the origin holds the request (Cloudflare cuts at 100s), then a sign-in page instead of a retry, which costs a Microsoft redirect round trip. Warm devices keep the cached shell.
fix: Add a 15s AbortController deadline to the /me fetch. In RoleGuard, when !loading && !user && error and an identity exists (msUser or a parent session), render an inline 'Could not reach Nexus' state with Retry (refreshAuth) and a secondary 'Sign in again'. Redirect only when there is no account or /me answered a real 401.
risk: LOW: an additive branch; the redirect stays for genuinely signed-out users.
expected: Every cold boot ends in content or a retryable error within about 15s.

history.note: fixed 2026-09-22 with a failing test first; uncommitted

title: The SWR cache is chosen once per page load, so View as Student and parent sign-in reuse the previous identity's cache
rootCause: The cache is created in a useState initialiser from the cached /me identity and never changes. SWR keys are bare URLs (the token is deliberately not in the key), so an identity change within a page load (start or exit impersonation, parent sign-in) keeps the same Map.
evidence: providers.tsx:38-43 `useState(() => ... createPersistentCache(readCachedAuth()?.oid ?? null))`. useNexusAuth.tsx:744-814 starts and exits impersonation without a reload. A teacher viewing as student A caches '/api/sketchbook/me?month=..'; viewing as student B within the 15s dedupe (providers.tsx:61) replays A's response.
impact: Staff using View as Student can see one student's work under another student's name, which misleads grading and support. Not a privilege gap: staff may see both.
fix: Move SWRConfig inside NexusAuthProvider and key it on the effective identity (ms, imp and parent). Give impersonation and parent sessions an in-memory Map, matching the writeCachedAuth rule that never persists those identities.
risk: MEDIUM: remounts the app subtree on identity switch, which already coincides with a route change.
expected: Each identity sees only its own cached reads.

title: Error boundaries: no app/error.tsx, none for (parent), (pad) or (auth), and global-error's 'Reload' only calls reset() and records nothing
rootCause: Only (teacher)/error.tsx and (student)/error.tsx exist, and a segment's error.tsx does not catch errors in its own layout. Everything else falls to global-error.tsx, which replaces the whole document, ignores the error, and remounts from the same localStorage state.
evidence: find apps/nexus/src/app -name error.tsx: (student)/error.tsx, (teacher)/error.tsx, global-error.tsx only. global-error.tsx:9 `GlobalError({ reset })`; :37-50 the 'Reload' button calls `reset()`; :34-35 student copy ('let your teacher know').
impact: A render error on a parent page, in the Answer Pad during class, on a login page, or in any shell component (TopBar, providers) replaces the whole app with a student-worded screen whose button can re-crash on the same cached data. Root crashes leave no trace.
fix: Add app/error.tsx (inside the root providers, role-neutral copy, Try again plus 'Clear saved data and reload') and (parent)/error.tsx inside the parent shell. Make global-error reload with window.location.reload() and log the message and digest.
risk: LOW: additive files. Run /ui-ux-pro-max for the new screens.
expected: A crash outside a page stays contained and recoverable, and root crashes become visible.

history.note: New app/error.tsx (role-neutral, inside root providers) and (parent)/error.tsx via components/RouteErrorScreen (Try again, clear saved data and reload, report only for signed-in staff/students); global-error.tsx reloads with window.location.reload(), offers clear-and-reload, logs message and digest, SVG icon instead of emoji. Tests: app/error.test.tsx, (parent)/error.test.tsx, global-error.test.tsx.

title: Sidebar and bottom-nav items are buttons calling router.push: no prefetch, no pending feedback and no link behaviour
rootCause: Every chrome navigation is router.push from onClick on ListItemButton or BottomNavigationAction. No next/link, no router.prefetch, no useTransition and no app loading.tsx exist in the chrome, so the router fetches the target's RSC payload and chunks only after the click, with the old page still on screen.
evidence: DesktopSidebar.tsx:152-154 `<ListItemButton ... onClick={() => router.push(item.path)}`; :396; BottomNav.tsx:117-121 and :305-307; TopBar.tsx:176; PanelProvider.tsx:166. grep finds no next/link, prefetch or useTransition in TopBar, DesktopSidebar or BottomNav; no loading.tsx under src/app.
impact: Every sidebar or bottom-nav navigation by every user looks dead until the payload and chunks arrive, worst on phones and on the first visit after a deploy (duration not measured). Rows also cannot be opened in a new tab and read as 'button' to screen readers.
fix: Render nav rows as links (`component={Link} href={item.path}`), keeping onClick only to close the More sheet. For remaining imperative pushes, wrap router.push in startTransition in a small hook and show a thin progress bar in TopBar while pending. Run /ui-ux-pro-max.
risk: MEDIUM: touches every nav row; check keyboard, focus and active styling. Prefetches of static routes are edge-served, not function invocations.
expected: Near-instant route swaps for prefetched routes and visible progress for the rest.

history.note: components/NavigationProgress: NavLink (next/link; plain clicks go through router.push inside a shared transition, modified clicks left to the browser), useNavigate, and a 3px top bar shown after 150ms of pending (static under reduced motion). DesktopSidebar rows, folder children, Course Plans rows and Home, and BottomNav tabs and More-sheet rows are links with aria-current; TopBar and PanelProvider pushes use useNavigate. All 117 fixed-path teacher/student/parent pages are static, so prefetch is CDN-served. Tests: NavigationProgress, DesktopSidebar, BottomNav.

title: The top-bar avatar URL is the same for every identity and cached publicly, so it can show the previous identity's photo
rootCause: `/api/graph/photo?size=48x48&self=true` carries no identity and answers `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`. GraphAvatar's in-memory cache key includes the impersonation identity, but the browser HTTP cache keys only on the URL.
evidence: route.ts:84 `'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400'`. GraphAvatar.tsx:93-95 selfIdentity; :145 `fetch(`/api/graph/photo?${params}`, { headers: { Authorization: ... } })` with no cache option.
impact: A teacher starting View as Student sees their own photo on the student's avatar. On a shared laptop the next person signed in within the hour can see the previous person's photo.
fix: Add the identity to the URL (for example `&for=<user or impersonated student id>`, ignored by the route) and send `private` instead of `public` on every branch of the route.
risk: LOW: a URL parameter and a header change; the browser cache still saves the request.
expected: The self avatar always matches the current identity.

title: Student stage facts are never refetched on a hard load while a saved copy exists
rootCause: The provider sets `revalidateIfStale: false`, so SWR skips the mount revalidation whenever cached data exists, and the persistent device cache supplies that data on every hard load. The persisted envelope has one savedAt that is rewritten on every flush, so the 24h limit never ages an individual entry out.
evidence: StudentStageFactsProvider.tsx:88-95 `useAuthSWR(STAGE_FACTS_KEY, { revalidateOnFocus: false, revalidateIfStale: false, dedupingInterval: 3_600_000, ... })`, whose comment says 'One request per session'. swr-cache.ts:188 `JSON.stringify({ savedAt: Date.now(), entries: ... })`.
impact: A student paused, restaged or marked for a language by one teacher keeps the old ring on other teachers' devices until a deploy, a reconnect or 24h of disuse. Visible on every avatar in the teacher app, with no error.
fix: Remove `revalidateIfStale: false`, which gives one background revalidation per hard load while the cached facts still paint first. Optionally give swr-cache per-entry timestamps.
risk: LOW: one extra request per hard load, which is the documented intent.
expected: Facts are at most one session old.

title: The bell's notification list has no deadline and shows a failed load as 'No notifications yet' with no retry
rootCause: Only the count poller got the 15s deadline (PERF-0011). The list fetch goes through fetchWithAuth with no signal, ignores !res.ok, swallows errors, and the hook exposes no error state.
evidence: useUserNotifications.ts:223 `return fetch(`${apiBaseUrl}${url}`, { ...init, headers })` with no signal; :242-251 `if (res?.ok) {...}` with no else; :252-253 `catch { // Silent fail }`. NotificationBell.tsx:411-421 renders spinner, 'No notifications yet' or the list.
impact: Anyone opening the bell while /api/notifications is slow or failing waits up to a 524, then reads 'No notifications yet' while the badge shows unread. The only retry is closing and reopening.
fix: Give the list fetch the same 15s AbortController as pollOnce, set and return an `error` on !ok or abort, and render 'Could not load notifications' with Retry in NotificationBell.
risk: MEDIUM: packages/ui is shared, so all four apps rebuild; the change is additive for their bells.
expected: The bell always ends in a list, an honest empty state or a retryable error within 15s.

title: The student activity heartbeat keeps posting from hidden and idle tabs: 54% of last week's rows record no activity
rootCause: The tracker starts a 1s tick and a 60s heartbeat and never stops them on visibilitychange. The tick keeps adding idle seconds while the tab is hidden, and sendHeartbeat skips only when both counters are zero.
evidence: useActiveTimeTracker.ts:103-112 tick; :115 `setInterval(sendHeartbeat, HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS)`; :118-136 the visibility handler stops neither interval; :44 `if (active === 0 && idle === 0) return;`. Measured on prod (device_activity_logs, last 7 days): 1,773 rows, 952 (53.7%) with active_seconds = 0, from 28 students. Each heartbeat costs verifyMsToken, a users read and about 3 device statements (api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:25-46).
impact: About half of the heartbeat invocations and rows record nothing but idle time. A hidden tab also calls getToken every minute, so a failed silent renewal could start a redirect in a tab nobody is looking at (inferred).
fix: On hidden, flush and stop both intervals; restart on visible, as NavBadgeProvider does. Do not count hidden time as idle, and skip the POST when active is 0, carrying idle seconds into the next active heartbeat.
risk: LOW: telemetry only; idle totals drop because hidden time stops counting as idle.
expected: Roughly half the heartbeat invocations and rows disappear, and hidden tabs send nothing.

history.note: useActiveTimeTracker stops both intervals while hidden, counts no hidden time, and sends a heartbeat only when a minute has active time; idle seconds ride along with the next active one. Test: useActiveTimeTracker.test.ts.

title: The page-hide heartbeat beacon carries no token, so the route always rejects it and those seconds are lost
rootCause: navigator.sendBeacon cannot set an Authorization header and the body has no token, while the heartbeat route requires the header. The counters are zeroed before the beacon is sent.
evidence: useActiveTimeTracker.ts:120-123 zeroes the counters; :125-134 `navigator.sendBeacon('/api/devices/heartbeat', JSON.stringify({ deviceId, sessionId, activeSeconds, idleSeconds }))`; tokenRef is used only as a gate. api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:20-23 `if (!authHeader || !deviceId) { return ... { status: 400 } }`.
impact: Every tab switch, app switch or screen lock after the first heartbeat fires a request that always returns 400, wasting an invocation and discarding up to 59s of counted time. Frequency not measured.
fix: Flush with `fetch(..., { method: 'POST', keepalive: true, headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + tokenRef.current, ... }, body })`, and zero the counters only when a token is available.
risk: LOW: same payload and route.
expected: Page-hide flushes are recorded and no invocation is spent on a guaranteed 400.

history.note: Page-hide flush is a keepalive fetch with the Authorization header instead of a header-less sendBeacon; the token is primed at start and counters are only taken when a token exists. Test: useActiveTimeTracker.test.ts.

title: View as Student registers the teacher's device and logs the teacher's time as the student's
rootCause: Device registration and the tracker run whenever isStudent is true, which includes impersonation, and getToken then returns the impersonation token that the server resolves as the student. Neither device route checks impersonatorUserId, unlike /api/auth/me.
evidence: DeviceRegistrationProvider.tsx:28-41 `useDeviceRegistration(getToken, isStudent, !authLoading)` and `enabled: !!deviceId && isStudent` with no impersonation check. api/devices/register/route.ts:38-64 and api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:25-46 never read impersonatorUserId, whereas api/auth/me/route.ts:195-209 deliberately writes nothing while impersonating. The registered-device id sits in an unscoped sessionStorage key (useDeviceRegistration.ts:37, :81) that signOut does not clear.
impact: A teacher viewing as a student can take that student's empty desktop slot with the teacher's fingerprint (the student's own desktop then gets the 'Unregistered Device' banner), and every minute of the session is logged as the student's active time.
fix: Pass `isStudent && !impersonation.active` to both hooks. In both device routes, return early without writing when msUser.impersonatorUserId is set. Key the sessionStorage entry by user id or clear it on sign-out.
risk: LOW: removes writes that should never happen; real students are unaffected.
expected: No device slots or activity rows written under impersonation.

history.note: DeviceRegistrationProvider passes isStudent && !impersonation.active to registration and tracking; /api/devices/register and /heartbeat write nothing when impersonatorUserId is set and now use errorResponse; the sessionStorage device id is stored as <userId>:<deviceId>. Tests: DeviceRegistrationProvider.test.tsx, devices/heartbeat and register route tests.

title: The heartbeat asks for geolocation from a timer, so students get an unexplained location prompt about a minute in
rootCause: sendHeartbeat calls navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition on every tick without checking the permission state, so the browser prompt appears with no user action and no explanation, and a pending prompt holds that heartbeat open.
evidence: useActiveTimeTracker.ts:55-68 `if (navigator.geolocation) { location = await new Promise((resolve) => { navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(..., { timeout: 5000, maximumAge: 300000 }) }) }`, inside the 60s interval (:115). No consent UI exists; no Permissions-Policy header restricts it.
impact: Every student whose browser has not decided yet sees 'wants to know your location' about a minute after opening Nexus, and again on later ticks until they answer.
fix: Read location only when navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'geolocation' }) reports 'granted'. If location is wanted, ask once from a user action with an explanation (for example in the profile Devices section).
risk: LOW: fewer location samples from students who never granted access.
expected: No unexplained permission prompts, and no heartbeat waits on a prompt.

history.note: Heartbeat reads location only when navigator.permissions reports geolocation 'granted', so no timer-driven prompt; no Permissions API means no location. Test: useActiveTimeTracker.test.ts.

title: nav-badges likely fires twice on a warm-cache hard load, because its effect is keyed on the user object
rootCause: The polling effect depends on `user`. The boot payload sets one user object and /api/auth/me then sets a new object for the same person, so the effect re-runs and polls again unless the first request is still in flight.
evidence: NavBadgeProvider.tsx:53 `const { getToken, user } = useNexusAuthContext();`, :119 `if (!user) return;`, :155 `}, [user, pollBadges]);`. useNexusAuth.tsx applies the boot payload user, then :591 `setUser(data.user)`.
impact: One extra /api/nav-badges request (about 14 queries for staff before PERF-0010) per warm hard load. Confirm with a HAR.
fix: Key the effect on `user?.id` instead of the object.
risk: LOW
expected: One badge request per hard load.

title: Staff with no active classroom enrolment get the student 'not in a classroom' screen on every page
rootCause: RoleGuard applies the classroom-membership rule to every role except parent, but the staff tier comes from staff_role or user_type, not from enrolments.
evidence: RoleGuard.tsx:111-112 `if (classrooms.length === 0) { return nexusRole === 'parent' ? <ParentNoChildLinked /> : <NoClassroomWelcome />; }`. me/route.ts:314-315 derives nexusRole from staffRole. Measured on prod: 24 of 30 staff accounts have no live classroom (23 of 25 teachers, 1 of 4 managers); none of them opened Nexus in the last 30 days.
impact: Latent today (no affected staff are active), but any staff member added without an enrolment cannot reach the Management or Admin panels and sees student marketing copy.
fix: A product decision first: if staff access is meant to be independent of enrolment, show NoClassroomWelcome only for students and let staff through (TopBar already hides the classroom chip with no active classroom), then check teacher pages cope with activeClassroom null.
risk: MEDIUM: some teacher pages may assume an active classroom.
expected: Staff access follows the staff tier.

history.note: User decided 2026-09-22: staff need a classroom, the same as students, so the RoleGuard rule stays. Staff with no classroom now get their own wording (added as a teacher by an admin: Classrooms, Teachers tab, Add Teacher) instead of the student welcome. Test: components/NoClassroomWelcome.test.tsx.

title: The next-pwa service worker is never registered on App Router pages, and its precache would fail to install
rootCause: next-pwa 5.6.0 injects its register script only into the Pages Router main.js entry; App Router pages do not load it. The generated precache also lists /_next/app-build-manifest.json, which Next does not serve.
evidence: Measured on production: none of the 19 chunks /login loads contain workbox or '/sw.js'; /sw.js is served (200, 459 precache entries); /_next/app-build-manifest.json returns 404. No app code calls serviceWorker.register.
impact: No stale-shell risk today, but the config and its comments describe caching that does not exist, and whoever enables registration inherits a failing install plus next-pwa's default reload-on-reconnect, which would hard-reload open exam pages when a phone regains signal.
fix: Remove next-pwa and its generated files (data caching already lives in SWR), or register explicitly with buildExcludes for app-build-manifest.json and reloadOnOnline: false.
risk: LOW: removing it matches current runtime behaviour exactly.
expected: Config matches reality; no latent reload-on-reconnect hazard.

title: The installed-app shortcut 'My Classrooms' opens a 404
rootCause: The shortcut url is /classrooms, a route that does not exist. The manifest name also uses an em dash, against the repo content rule.
evidence: manifest.json:44-50 `"url": "/classrooms"`; GET https://nexus.neramclasses.com/classrooms returns 404 (measured).
impact: Anyone who installed Nexus and long-presses the icon lands on a 404.
fix: Point the shortcut at an existing route (for example '/') or remove it, and rename to 'Nexus: Neram Classroom'.
risk: LOW
expected: A working shortcut.

title: The auth boot cache is not keyed by build, so a new deploy's first frame renders the previous build's /me payload
rootCause: The storage key has no build stamp, unlike swr-cache, and clearPersistentCache does not clear it, so the error boundary's 'clear saved data' also leaves it.
evidence: auth-cache.ts:23 `const KEY = 'nexus_auth_cache_v1';`. useNexusAuth.tsx:362-380 applies the cached payload before paint on any build.
impact: Bounded (fields have fallbacks and /me replaces them in one round trip), but a future payload shape change can crash the first frame after a deploy.
fix: Store NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_STAMP in the entry and treat a different stamp as absent, or validate the shape before applying.
risk: LOW
expected: No cross-build payload drives rendering.

title: The photo gate, image cropper and alumni screen ship in the root bundle of every route
rootCause: AccessGate, mounted for every route, statically imports AlumniAccessEnded and PhotoRequiredGate, which pulls in ProfilePhotoUpload and react-easy-crop, although they render only for graduated or photo-blocked students.
evidence: AccessGate.tsx:4-5 static imports; ProfilePhotoUpload.tsx:23 `import Cropper from 'react-easy-crop'` (8.5 KB gzip, file size measured; route cost not measured).
impact: Every user downloads and parses code almost no one uses.
fix: next/dynamic both gates inside AccessGate.
risk: LOW
expected: Smaller shared first-load JS (not measured).

title: A render-blocking Google Material Icons stylesheet loads on every route for 4 pages that use it
rootCause: The fonts.googleapis.com Material Icons stylesheet is linked in the root head, but only the checklist and modules pages use className='material-icons'.
evidence: layout.tsx:51-54 `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Icons">`, present in production HTML (measured). grep finds material-icons in 4 pages only.
impact: On a cold visit, first paint on every route waits on a cross-origin DNS, TLS and CSS round trip (not measured).
fix: Load it only on those pages, or map the module icon names to @mui/icons-material SVGs.
risk: LOW
expected: One fewer render-blocking request on about 180 routes.

title: PanelProvider always starts on 'teaching', so hard loads of Management and Admin routes paint the wrong nav first
rootCause: The initial panel is a constant; the saved panel is applied in one effect and the URL panel in a second effect gated on `hydrated`, a render later. PanelProvider renders only under RoleGuard, so deriving it synchronously from the pathname is safe.
evidence: PanelProvider.tsx:111 `useState<PanelId>('teaching')`; :131-141 localStorage in an effect; :143-155 `if (!hydrated) return; const detected = detectPanelFromPath(pathname)`.
impact: Staff hard-loading /teacher/students or /teacher/admin/* see the sidebar, bottom tabs and classroom chip swap after first paint.
fix: Initialise from detectPanelFromPath(pathname) when it is set and allowed, and apply the saved panel only when the path names none.
risk: LOW
expected: The first shell frame shows the right panel.

title: View-as-Student search can show an older query's results over a newer one, and a failed load reads 'No students available'
rootCause: fetchCandidates has no AbortController or request id, so an older response can land last; the error shows only in a 6s Snackbar, after which the empty message appears.
evidence: ViewAsStudentDialog.tsx:69-78 `setResults(data.students || [])` unguarded; :82-83 `finally { setLoading(false) }`; :100-104 400ms debounce; :307-309 `autoHideDuration={6000}`.
impact: Staff typing a name on a slow connection can see the wrong list and pick the wrong student; a failed load reads as 'no students'.
fix: Keep a request id ref or abort the previous request on each call and on close; render the error inline with Retry.
risk: LOW
expected: Only the latest query's results show, and failures are recoverable.

title: Report-an-issue buttons wait on an unbounded full-page screenshot with no feedback on the crash screens
rootCause: Both error boundaries await captureScreenshot() before opening the dialog; the capture renders document.body with modern-screenshot's default 30s per-asset timeout, and the button has no pending state or re-entry guard.
evidence: (teacher)/error.tsx:52-56 and (student)/error.tsx:37-41 `const shot = await captureScreenshot(); setAutoShot(shot); setOpen(true);`; buttons never disabled. capture-screenshot.ts:18 `domToBlob(document.body, { ... })` with no timeout.
impact: A user reporting a crash taps a button that looks dead for a while (longer on phones and heavy pages); repeat taps start parallel captures.
fix: Race the capture against about 3s and open the dialog without a picture if it loses; add a capturing state that disables the button, as ReportIssueFab does.
risk: LOW
expected: The report dialog opens within about 3s.

title: Chrome and banner controls lack accessible names, one hides its focus ring, and the bell is a 32px target
rootCause: Icon-only buttons have no aria-label, the classroom switcher removes its outline with no focus-visible replacement, the device banner's action is a clickable span, and the RoleGuard spinner is not a live region.
evidence: NotificationBell.tsx:372 `<IconButton onClick={handleOpen} size="small" ...>` (no aria-label, about 32px); TopBar.tsx:157-158 hamburger with no aria-label; TopBar.tsx:249 and :272 `outline: 'none'`; DeviceLimitBanner.tsx:50-62 `<Box component='span' onClick=...>` and :34-36 unnamed close; RoleGuard.tsx:81-95 spinner with no role='status'.
impact: Screen-reader users hear 'button' for the bell on every page, keyboard users lose focus on the classroom switcher, and the device-swap action cannot be reached by keyboard.
fix: Add aria-labels (bell with unread count), 44px targets, a focus-visible outline, a real Button or Link for the banner action, and role='status' on the spinner. Run /ui-ux-pro-max.
risk: LOW
expected: The shell meets the repo's accessibility bar.

title: Parents' top bar requests a Microsoft Graph photo with the parent token on every load, which always fails
rootCause: TopBar hides the bell for parents but still renders GraphAvatar self; the photo route forwards the parent token to Graph, which answers 401, and GraphAvatar caches only 404s.
evidence: TopBar.tsx:401 hides the bell for parents; :433-438 and :560 render `<GraphAvatar self />` for every role. api/graph/photo/route.ts:55-70 forwards the token to Graph and passes its 401 through. GraphAvatar.tsx:149-152 caches only 404.
impact: Every parent load and profile-menu open costs an invocation and a Graph round trip that cannot succeed, and sends the parent session token to Graph.
fix: Skip the self fetch for parents (use avatar_url or initials), and have the route return 404 for parent tokens before calling Graph.
risk: LOW
expected: Parents make no photo requests.

title: Device registration has no in-flight guard, so a double run can show a false device-limit banner
rootCause: The register effect has no cleanup or shared promise, and the sessionStorage gate is written only after success; the server's check-then-insert reports a unique-index collision (23505) as a limit error.
evidence: useDeviceRegistration.ts:31-99 effect with no cleanup; :81 writes sessionStorage after response.ok; :84-89 sets limitReached on 409. packages/database/src/queries/device-registration.ts:86-99 returns isLimitError on '23505'.
impact: Rare in production (needs a re-run while the first request is in flight); in dev Strict Mode every new tab registers twice.
fix: Share one registration per page through a module-level in-flight promise, and on 23505 re-read the row by fingerprint instead of reporting a limit.
risk: LOW
expected: One register call per tab session and no false banner.

title: A stalled issue-report submit traps the student in a dialog they cannot close
rootCause: The final POST has no deadline and closing is refused while submitting.
evidence: ReportIssueDialog.tsx:154-169 `await fetch('/api/foundation/issues', { method: 'POST', ... })` with no signal; :190-195 `handleClose = () => { if (!submitting) { ... } }`.
impact: During a slow request the student sees 'Submitting...' in a modal with no way out.
fix: Add signal: AbortSignal.timeout(20000) and show the existing error snackbar on abort; allow closing by aborting.
risk: LOW
expected: Submit always ends in success or a retryable error within about 20s.

title: Photo gate gives no feedback when the refresh after an upload fails
rootCause: handleUploaded awaits refreshAuth(); if /me fails the context sets `error`, which the gate never reads, so the gate stays up.
evidence: PhotoRequiredGate.tsx:58-64 `setSubmitted(true); setOpen(false); await refreshAuth();`.
impact: A student who just uploaded stays blocked with no explanation or retry.
fix: After the refresh, read `error` and show an Alert with 'Check again' calling refreshAuth.
risk: LOW
expected: A recoverable state after a failed refresh.

title: Small hygiene in the bell and image helper: a div inside a p, and an object URL never revoked
rootCause:
ListItemText wraps a non-Typography `secondary` in a

while the content is a Box (div); compressImage creates an object URL it never revokes.
evidence: NotificationBell.tsx:461-462 `secondary={ <Box> ... }`; lib/image-compress.ts:33 `img.src = URL.createObjectURL(file);` with no revoke.
impact: A dev console error on every bell open (client-only, so not a hydration failure), and one or two screenshot blobs retained per report.
fix: Add `secondaryTypographyProps={{ component: 'div' }}`; revoke the URL in onload and onerror.
risk: LOW
expected: Clean console; no retained blobs.

title: The root layout ships the Firebase Auth SDK and server-only Graph helpers to every Nexus route through the @neram/auth barrel
rootCause: useNexusAuth imports from the '@neram/auth' barrel, which re-exports ./firebase, ./microsoft, ./graph and ./hooks. The package declares no sideEffects and is not in optimizePackageImports, and firebase/app and firebase/auth register themselves at import, so webpack keeps them. Nexus never uses Firebase.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:4 `import { useMicrosoftAuth, getAccessToken, getAccessTokenSilent, loginScopes } from '@neram/auth';`. packages/auth/src/index.ts re-exports './firebase' and './graph'. next.config.js:74 optimizePackageImports lists only '@neram/ui' and MUI. packages/auth/package.json exports './hooks': './src/hooks.ts' but the file is hooks.tsx. Measured on the local production build (BUILD_ID czq59NBfmlgbnYo9PkESe): the root '/layout' loads 15 JS files (1,405,648 B raw, 395,137 B gzip), and static/chunks/390bae33-ddd74102616385ea.js (98,195 B raw, 28,089 B gzip) contains identitytoolkit.googleapis.com.
impact: Every Nexus page load, on every device, downloads, parses and runs the Firebase Auth SDK (about 28 KB gzip in one chunk, more in others) plus dead Graph admin helpers. Most costly on the low-end Android phones students use (parse time not measured).
fix: App-scoped: add '@neram/auth' to experimental.optimizePackageImports in apps/nexus/next.config.js. Package-level: import from '@neram/auth/microsoft' and '@neram/auth/hooks' after correcting the exports map to './src/hooks.tsx' (a packages/ change rebuilds all four apps). Verify that no '/layout' chunk contains identitytoolkit.googleapis.com.
risk: LOW: only import paths change; the MSAL code is identical.
expected: About 28 KB gzip or more less JavaScript on every route.

history.note: App-scoped: '@neram/auth' added to experimental.optimizePackageImports in apps/nexus/next.config.js; no packages/ change. Guard: tests/guardrails/nexus-auth-barrel.test.ts.

Measured on local production build txFLQty6DdqLDvKFNzgya vs czq59NBfmlgbnYo9PkESe: root /layout JS 15 files 1,405,648 B raw / 395,137 B gzip -> 13 files 1,230,075 B raw / 343,861 B gzip (-51,276 B gzip, -13%). No /layout chunk and no page in app-build-manifest lists the Firebase chunk; it survives only as a lazy chunk nothing in Nexus loads.

title: When a session expires, a background poll's getToken can start a full-page Microsoft redirect under the user
rootCause: getToken always calls the redirecting getAccessToken, which on InteractionRequiredAuthError calls acquireTokenRedirect from whichever caller hit it first, including the 60s badge and bell pollers. The context has no silent getter and no 'session expired' state.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:439 `return getAccessToken(loginScopes.nexus);`. packages/auth/src/microsoft.ts:446-452 `if (error instanceof InteractionRequiredAuthError) { return redirectForTokenOnce(msal, scopes, account); }`. Background callers: NavBadgeProvider.tsx:67 `await getToken()` on a 60s interval; NotificationBell passes getToken to the 60s notifications poller; the student heartbeat calls it every minute (PERF-0033).
impact: When silent renewal fails (refresh token expiry, or browsers blocking third-party cookies such as Safari and iOS), the next poll navigates the whole page to login.microsoftonline.com. A teacher typing feedback or a student mid-answer loses unsaved input with no warning. Frequency not measured.
fix: Give background callers a silent getter (getAccessTokenSilent already exists). When it fails with interaction required, set a `sessionExpired` flag that shows a non-blocking 'Your session expired. Sign in again' prompt whose button calls getAccessToken. Move NavBadgeProvider, useUserNotifications and the heartbeat to the silent getter.
risk: MEDIUM: foreground callers keep today's behaviour; pollers stop refreshing until the user acts.
expected: An expired session never navigates away under the user.

history.note: Context gains getTokenSilently (signInSilent: null means interaction required -> sessionExpired; a throw is a plain null), sessionExpired and renewSession. NavBadgeProvider, NotificationBell's poller and the device registration/heartbeat use the silent getter; SessionExpiredPrompt (root providers) shows a non-blocking, dismissible prompt. Tests: useNexusAuth.session-expired, NavBadgeProvider, NotificationBell, DeviceRegistrationProvider, SessionExpiredPrompt. Not moved (outside the finding): test-take autosave, usePresence, useWatchTracker, useVideoProgress, ExamInvigilationRoster.

title: Starting or exiting View as Student leaves the context on the old identity with loading false, so guards bounce and Exit loses its return page
rootCause: `booted` is set once at boot and never cleared, so after boot `loading` ignores the /me reload that each identity change starts. Role, classrooms and user still describe the old identity while getToken already returns the new token. refreshAuth's load cannot be cancelled either, so a late refresh can overwrite a newer identity.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:932 `loading: user && booted ? false : ...`; `booted` is set only at boot. :785 `setImpersonationState(stored)` then :524 `setDbLoading(true)` is masked by :932. ViewAsStudentButton.tsx:64-65 `await startImpersonation(...); router.push('/student/dashboard');`. RoleGuard.tsx:62-65 redirects when nexusRole is not allowed. ImpersonationBanner.tsx:40-48 pushes returnUrl after exitImpersonation. :711-713 `loadNexusUser(() => false)`.
impact: Staff with a warm device cache who start View as Student can bounce student, teacher, student while /me reloads, and on Exit land on the student dashboard and then /teacher/dashboard instead of where they started. Meanwhile pages fire requests with the student's token.
fix: Treat an identity change as a fresh boot: in startImpersonation, clearImpersonation and parentLogin, reset `booted` and bootedRef so `loading` covers the reload. Add a load sequence ref so only the latest load may write state.
risk: LOW: a spinner during the switch; boot behaviour unchanged.
expected: The switch lands once on the right screen, and Exit returns to the page it came from.

history.note: useNexusAuth: startImpersonation, exit/auto-exit/4xx exit (endImpersonation) and parentLogin call beginIdentitySwitch (reset booted, raise dbLoading, bump the load sequence); loadNexusUser writes only when it is the newest load. Test: hooks/useNexusAuth.identity-switch.test.tsx (warm cache: loading covers start and exit; a late refresh cannot restore the old identity).

title: useWatchTracker creates a second full useNexusAuth instance, adding a /api/auth/me call and a users-row write per library video open
rootCause: The raw useNexusAuth hook is exported and called directly instead of reading the provider's context, which creates a second MSAL hook, boot effect and /me load.
evidence: useWatchTracker.ts:71 `const { getToken, user } = useNexusAuth();`, used by app/(student)/student/library/[videoId]/page.tsx. The second instance runs loadNexusUser (useNexusAuth.tsx:538) and writeCachedAuth (:633). /me runs a users UPDATE for the login stamp plus enrolment, batch and settings reads (me/route.ts:236-259).
impact: Every student library video open repeats the heaviest shell request, including a DB write, and holds a second copy of identity state that ignores changes made through the context.
fix: Use useNexusAuthContext() in useWatchTracker, and stop exporting the raw hook (or restrict it with a lint rule) so the provider is the only owner.
risk: LOW: same values from the shared instance.
expected: One /api/auth/me call per boot, app-wide.

title: Parent sign-out bounces between /parent/login and /parent/dashboard while the logout call is pending, then lands on the Microsoft login page
rootCause: signOut clears `user` at once but keeps the parent session until an awaited logout fetch (no deadline) settles. In between, RoleGuard (user null) and the parent login page (session still active) redirect to each other.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:828 `setUser(null)`; :854-857 `await fetch('/api/auth/parent/logout', ...)` with no signal; only then :861-862 `clearParentSession(); setParentSession(null);`. RoleGuard.tsx:45-58 pushes '/parent/login'; parent/login/page.tsx:48-52 replaces back to '/parent/dashboard'. TopBar.tsx:117-121 `await signOut(); router.push('/login');`.
impact: Every parent sign-out flickers between two routes for the length of the logout call, and a hung call extends it; the parent then ends on the Microsoft sign-in page, which is not theirs.
fix: Capture the token, clear the parent session synchronously with the rest of the reset, send the logout best effort (keepalive plus a timeout, not awaited), and route parents to /parent/login after sign-out.
risk: LOW: the server-side token_version bump is still attempted.
expected: Parent sign-out finishes at once, on /parent/login.

title: A boot payload from an older build shows new default-off features as enabled until /me answers
rootCause: The boot path applies the cached, already-resolved flag map as is, and isFeatureEnabled treats an id missing from the map as enabled.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:372 `setFeatureFlags(payload.featureFlags ?? resolveFlags({}))`. feature-flags.ts:378-381 `if (!f) return true; return flags[id] !== false;`. resolveFlags fills defaults for missing ids.
impact: On the first open after a deploy that adds a default-off student feature, students with a warm cache see and can reach it for one /me round trip (the whole session if /me fails).
fix: `setFeatureFlags(resolveFlags(payload.featureFlags ?? {}))` so ids missing from an older map get their registry defaults.
risk: LOW: one line; identical output for known ids.
expected: A cached shell never enables a feature the current build has off.

title: Each device-cache flush stringifies the whole SWR cache twice on the main thread, and a failed write leaves an old snapshot
rootCause: serialise() stringifies every persistable entry to measure it, then stringifies the kept set again, re-stringifying oversized entries only to drop them. Map insertion order is treated as recency although SWR's set on an existing key keeps its position. A failed setItem leaves the previous payload.
evidence: swr-cache.ts:163 `Array.from(map.entries()).reverse()`; :172 `JSON.stringify([key, ...])`; :178 `if (encoded.length > MAX_ENTRY_BYTES) continue;`; :188 second stringify; the set wrapper schedules a flush (1s debounce) on every persistable set; :224-229 swallows setItem failure.
impact: About 1s after every navigation or revalidation burst and on every tab hide, up to about 4 MB of JSON.stringify plus a synchronous setItem of up to 2 MB run on the main thread (not measured). Over budget, the oldest-inserted (often most-used) reads are dropped.
fix: Remember each entry's encoded size so unchanged entries are not re-stringified, delete-then-set so order means recency, build the output once, remove the bucket on setItem failure, and optionally flush in requestIdleCallback.
risk: LOW: internal to the module; existing tests cover behaviour.
expected: Flush cost proportional to what changed.

title: PERF-0001 gap: impersonation, parent and test sessions are still read from storage in useState initialisers (latent #418)
rootCause: The PERF-0001 fix moved only the boot payload into the layout effect; three other storage reads stay in useState initialisers, so tokenReady, impersonation and parentSession differ between the server render and the first client render for those sessions.
evidence: useNexusAuth.tsx:384-386 `useState(() => readStoredImpersonation())`, :391-393 `useState(() => readParentSession())`, :458-461 test token. :934 tokenReady differs server vs client. auth-cache.ts:49-50 still says 'Safe to call during a useState initialiser'. Masked today because `loading` is true on both sides and RoleGuard shows the same spinner.
impact: No mismatch today. Any future consumer that renders these above RoleGuard's spinner brings #418 and #423 back for every parent and every View as Student hard load.
fix: Start the three as null or false and read them in the same layout effect as the boot payload; correct the auth-cache.ts comment.
risk: LOW: current consumers sit behind loading.
expected: The first client render matches the server for every identity type.

title: The reported-questions inbox fails on every load: its users embed is ambiguous and names a column that does not exist
rootCause: listOpenRecapQuestionReports embeds `student:users(full_name, avatar_url)`. nexus_class_recap_question_reports has two foreign keys to users (student_id and resolved_by), so PostgREST cannot choose one (PGRST201), and users has no full_name column (it is `name`).
evidence: Prod catalog: two FKs to users, no users.full_name. Staging PostgREST: old select returns HTTP 300 PGRST201; the fixed select returns 200. Prod console 2026-09-24: GET /api/class-recaps/question-reports 500 on every catch-up load. RecapReviewQueue.tsx:124 turns the rejection into an empty list.
impact: A 500 on every teacher load of Catch-up, and any student 'report a mistake' would never reach a teacher (prod has 0 reports so far, so none were lost).
fix: Embed `users!nexus_class_recap_question_reports_student_id_fkey(name, avatar_url)` and map student_name from `name`. Route: check the classrooms read and classify errors with httpStatusForError.
risk: LOW: one select string and one field mapping, pinned by unit tests.
expected: GET /api/class-recaps/question-reports answers 200 and lists open reports.

title: Timetable, class-insights and timetable-notifications report a failed read as 404 'not found' and an expired token as 500
rootCause: `.single()` reads keep only `data` and drop `error`, so a timeout or dropped proxy connection returns 404 'User not found' / 'Class not found in this classroom'. class-insights also dropped the errors of its attendance, RSVP, absences and away-window reads, so a failed attendance read looked like an unsynced class. The catch blocks answered 500 for everything, including 'Missing or invalid Authorization header'.
evidence: Prod 2026-09-24: class-insights 404 for class 1f97a143 in classroom 8876a8fc, which exists in that classroom (verified on prod), and no ms_oid is duplicated. Same minute: /api/timetable 404, /api/timetable/notifications 500 x2, /api/notifications 500 (that route classifies errors, so its 500 is a real database failure). Vercel runtime logs returned 403 and the Supabase logs API is retired, so response bodies were not read.
impact: One database blip reads as 'this class does not exist' and an empty week, and a lapsed session reads as a server error the client cannot recover from.
fix: New throwIfReadFailed(error, what) in lib/api-errors.ts: PGRST116 passes, anything else throws ApiError 503. Applied to every read on these paths, and the catches use httpStatusForError + messageOf.
risk: LOW: status codes change only on the failure paths; tests pin 404 for a real missing row.
expected: A failed read answers 503, a missing row 404, an expired token 401.

title: Class drawer Attended and Missed tabs hold skeletons over a failed or hung load, with no error and no retry
rootCause: fetchWithToken had no deadline on getToken() or fetch, so a hang kept SWR's isLoading true for good. ClassAttendancePanel never read `error`, and the tabs branched only on insightsLoading then !insights, so a failure showed skeletons through SWR's retries and then an info note with nothing to press.
evidence: Prod screenshot 2026-09-24: Attended tab on three skeletons while class-insights had answered 404.
impact: A teacher cannot tell a failed load from a slow one and has to close the drawer to try again.
fix: fetchWithToken: 20s deadline covering the token and the request, surfacing NexusFetchError 408. Panel passes insightsError, insightsRetrying and onRetryInsights; both tabs render the new InsightsLoadError (error Alert with role=alert, 48px Try again) before the loading branch.
risk: LOW: shared fetcher gains a deadline only; all 6793 related tests pass.
expected: A failed load shows the route's message and Try again at once; a hang becomes that error within 20s.

title: The catch-up class drawer reads insights with the widest teacher token
rootCause: ClassAttendancePanel gets getTeacherToken (loginScopes.nexusTeacher, including Group.ReadWrite.All and Calendars.ReadWrite) for its reads as well as for Sync from Teams, which does need the delegated token (attendance-report route:295). If the wider set cannot be refreshed silently, a read-only view triggers a full-page redirect, or after a recent redirect sends no token at all.
evidence: packages/auth/src/microsoft.ts getAccessToken -> redirectForTokenOnce returns null within 60s of a previous redirect; fetchWithToken then sends no Authorization header.
impact: A read-only drawer can bounce the teacher to Microsoft or fail with 401 when only the write scopes are the problem.
fix: Add an optional getReadToken prop to ClassAttendancePanel for useClassInsights and the register read, and pass getToken from the catch-up drawer; keep getTeacherToken for Sync from Teams and nudges.
risk: LOW, but touches files another session is editing; deferred until that work lands.
expected: Reads never need the teacher-only scopes.
